newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African wool prices rise at latest auction.
newsitem.headline: S.African wool prices rise at latest auction.

text.p: South African wool prices were higher at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said.
It said 11,960 bales were offered at this week's sale, of which 98.0 percent was sold.

Price quotes for long Merino fleeces of 20 micron rose 2.8 percent, 21 micron fell 0.3 percent, 22 micron rose 1.3 percent, 23 micron rose 1.3 percent, 24 micron rose 1.6 percent and 25 micron rose 0.4 percent.
Prices for Merino bellies rose 1.3 percent, Merino lambs rose 3.6 percent and Merino locks rose 1.1 percent.
The offering included 1,906 bales of other White Wools, 1,462 bales of Ciskei/Transkei, 2,161 bales of Lesotho and 1,207 bales of coarse and coloured.

Of the 933 bales of 20 micron offered, 96.5 percent was sold. Of the 2,029 bales of 21 micron offered, 98.7 percent was sold. Of the 1,777 bales of 22 micron offered, 99.0 percent was sold. Of the 1,285 bales of 23 micron offered, 98.9 percent was sold and of the 402 bales of 24 micron offered, 98.0 percent was sold. All of the 25 micron bales were sold.
The next sale will take place on March 12, when 8,900 bales will be on offer.
